channel.title: Farmer's Weekly SA - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Farmer's Weekly SA (farmersweekly.co.za)

item.title: Sugar industry crisis prompts call for state intervention
item.description: The South African Canegrowers Association has written to President Cyril Ramaphosa and several Cabinet ministers, requesting urgent action to prevent the liquidation of Tongaat Hulett and stabilise the wider sugar industry.

item.title: Leading African agribusinesses gather in Gqeberha for IBMA 2026
item.description: The 2026 International Conference on Business Models in Agriculture is taking place from 8 to 10 March at The Boardwalk Hotel and Convention Centre in Gqeberha, Eastern Cape. This year’s theme is ‘AgriFuture: Connecting African Innovation to Global Markets’.

item.title: Agri sector calls for fair taxes, policy certainty in Budget 2026
item.description: As Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana prepares to table the 2026 National Budget this afternoon, agricultural stakeholders say his speech will reveal whether government is serious about protecting jobs, managing risk, and supporting the sector’s long-term growth.

item.title: Healing the soil to survive the droughts
item.description: On Nooitgedacht farm near Kenhardt in the Northern Cape, drought isn’t a crisis – it’s a way of life. But by improving soil health, Charl Saunderson has managed to make his land more resilient and productive in one of South Africa’s toughest farming regions.

item.title: Budget 2026: debt stabilises, growth remains muted
item.description: South Africa’s economic growth outlook is steadily improving, with growth projected to reach 1,6% in 2026, up from 1,4% in 2025. Growth is expected to average 1,8% over the medium term, reaching 2% by 2028.

item.title: Dairy processors, producers unite against ‘disproportionate’ FMD rules
item.description: South Africa’s dairy industry has warned that inconsistent and non-standardised foot-and-mouth disease controls are placing it under mounting strain, despite scientific consensus that properly processed dairy products are safe for human consumption.

item.title: Smarter selection, stronger animals: how AI is changing livestock genetics
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is no longer a future concept in livestock breeding. Benefits are already being seen in the speed and accuracy of selection programmes, bringing improvements in longevity, efficiency, and welfare.

item.title: Join us at the 2026 Malanseuns Garden Festival!
item.description: Get ready to dig in, explore, and be inspired! The third annual Malanseuns Garden Festival, taking place from 10 to 12 April, promises a vibrant weekend filled with lush displays, hands-on learning, and outdoor fun for all ages.

item.title: Gauteng scales up FMD vaccination as cases climb to 228
item.description: Gauteng’s battle against foot-and-mouth disease has entered what provincial authorities describe as its ‘most decisive phase’, with a scaled-up vaccination programme launched on 26 February as the number of confirmed cases continues to rise.

item.title: Budget 2026: agriculture gets support, but biosecurity gaps remain
item.description: The response to the 2026 Budget Speech, delivered in Parliament on Wednesday by Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana, was largely positive. However, the absence of specific support to address the foot-and-mouth disease outbreak has left the sector feeling discouraged.
